cells.tense: What you released for is being seen and valued right here, and you are at the pen as it gets marked.
cells.act: tend the resource with responsible care
cells.ask: Keep carrying what you have almost finished, steady for one more week, then set it down for good. The setting down is the last step, and nothing follows it.
cells.core:
What you let go of to get here is being seen and valued now, and you're at the pen when the mark lands. A cycle is closing. It feels nearly as solid as the work did, and it should, because the steady care turned into something made, and the made thing got noticed.

Here is that same care in smaller form. Keep carrying what you have almost finished, steady for one more week, then set it down for good. Not because finishing is risky, but because setting it down is where you find out the thing is finished. The week proves it to the hands. Setting it down makes it true.
cells.sheetLine: What you released for is being seen, and the cycle can close.
cells.verb: carrying a thing through, then letting it be seen and marked
cells.place: the doorstep where finished work is handed over and left behind

cells.tense: You are bracing for a looking-at that no one can arrange, and pushing at it before its hour.
cells.act: sort what matters from what does not, carefully
cells.ask: Take the work you mean to finish and make one clean cut: keep what matters, strike what doesn't, and put nothing back on the list.
cells.core:
You're bracing for a looking-at that can't be arranged, so you've started arranging it — finishing early, tightening the thing nobody has seen yet, rehearsing. Your energy goes to managing the response instead of finishing the work, and the end keeps sliding a day out. Something that was going to be seen has turned into something that must be proved.

Make one clean cut before you start. Take the work you mean to finish, keep what matters, strike what doesn't, and put nothing back on the list. One distinction first, the way you clear a bench before real work. Refining that serves the work feels quiet. If the cutting is winding you tighter, you're cutting for the wrong pair of eyes, and your hands will tell you which.
cells.sheetLine: The finish line moves because you're bracing for someone to look.

cells.tense: The release already happened and you are at the door that closed behind you, still asking whether it counted.
cells.act: persist on your own reserves through the pressure
cells.ask: Carry your own share of one task this week the whole way on what you have left, no stocking up, and afterward skip checking whether it was enough.
cells.core:
The release already happened. You're at the door that closed behind you, still asking whether it counted, and the asking is the part with no end in it. You keep turning up; your hands know the way. What's missing is the moment the thing was handed over and allowed to be over. Inside, nothing confirms the effort landed anywhere, so no finish feels finished.

Carry your own share of one task this week the whole way on what you have left, no stocking up first, and afterward skip checking whether it was enough. That's how you learn the reserves are still there — not by feeling strong, by spending them on something small while nobody watches. Strength comes back by being used, not by waiting until you feel you have it.

cells.tense: Your hands keep completing the work and handing it on, yet the one who put in the years is not the one you name.
cells.act: look after what grows with a steady hand
cells.ask: Write your name where the receipt goes — the log, the note, the record — before the thing you've raised leaves your hands.
cells.core:
Work keeps getting finished and passed on, and the one who put in the years isn't who you'd name if someone asked. The upkeep runs anyway — the materials, the maintenance, the putting in — and it runs well while your account of it stays thin. You'd say it's just keeping things going. Keeping this going has taken years of one person's attention.

Write your name where the receipt goes before the thing you've raised leaves your hands. The log, the note, the record, wherever the finished thing gets noted down. Not a claim, just a mark. Being recorded is where the credit returns, and you can start smaller than a ceremony. The work has been getting done. The page is where you learn it was yours.
cells.sheetLine: The work completes under your hands. The record could say so.
